0.desc: Spectrum Management Measurement Request (category 0, action 0). Asks the target to measure a channel and report back. Low hit rate on modern supplicants; mostly airtime noise.

1.desc: Transmit Power Control Request (category 0, action 1). Asks the target to report its transmit power. Very rarely honored; useful only as a fingerprinting probe.

2.desc: Spectrum Management Channel Switch Announcement (category 0, action 4). Beacon CSA delivered as an action frame. Some clients only parse the action form.

3.desc: Public Action (category 4, action 10) — GAS Initial Request with an ANQP Venue Name query. Loads the AP's management plane if aimed at the AP; low impact if aimed at a client.

4.desc: Public Action (category 4, action 11) — GAS Comeback Request. Resumes a fragmented GAS exchange. Flooded against an AP it never queried is mostly noise.

5.desc: Public Action (category 4, action 4) — Extended Channel Switch Announcement as an action frame. Same effect as beacon CSA but wrapped differently; hits clients that reject beacon CSA.

6.desc: Public Action (category 4, action 14) — TDLS Discovery Response. Only meaningful between two STAs; ignored by APs.

7.desc: Radio Measurement Request (category 5, action 0) with a Beacon Measurement subtype. Wastes client radio time; occasionally triggers reassociation on stale results.

8.desc: Radio Measurement Request (category 5, action 0) with a Link Measurement subtype. Asks the client to measure the AP's signal quality. Low disruption; fingerprint value only.

9.desc: Radio Measurement Request (category 5, action 0) with a Neighbor Report subtype. Forces the AP to enumerate neighbors; small mgmt-plane load.

10.desc: Fast BSS Transition Auth Request (category 6, action 1). 802.11r FT authentication. Pick a variant below.

basic.desc: Minimal FT Auth Request: algo/seq/status + stub FTE + stub MIE. Broadest compatibility, weakest parse-through.

full.desc: FT Auth Request with a proper Mobility Domain Element and a fuller FTE structure. Gets past stricter parsers that reject malformed FTEs.

11.desc: Fast BSS Transition Action Request (category 6, action 2). Pre-roam neighbor query. Abused to make a client prepare a roam to a dead BSSID.

12.desc: SA Query Request (category 8, action 0). PMF-specific path that still reaches clients on 802.11w networks — forged requests confuse some supplicants into dropping the link, bypassing the usual deauth block.

13.desc: SA Query Response (category 8, action 1). Normally the client's reply. Spoofed responses to a real SA Query can make the AP think the client is a MitM and drop it.

14.desc: WNM BSS Transition Management Request (category 10, action 7). Makes 802.11v-capable clients roam away from the real AP. Pick a variant below.

basic.desc: Single forged neighbor pointing to a fake BSSID on channel 1. Simplest form.

multi.desc: 2-3 forged neighbors on random common channels. Matches the shape of real enterprise BTM Requests — highest hit rate on modern clients.

disassoc.desc: BTM Request with the Disassociation Imminent bit and a 10 TU timer. Forces clients that honor BTM to leave fast.

15.desc: WNM BSS Transition Management Query (category 10, action 6). Client asking the AP for BTM candidates. Spoofed against an AP is mostly noise; spoofed against a client confuses its BTM state.

16.desc: WNM BSS Transition Management Response (category 10, action 8). Normally the client's reply to a BTM Request. Spoofed to an AP it can desynchronize the AP's view of the client's roam state.

17.desc: WNM Channel Usage Request (category 10, action 9). Asks the client to report channel occupancy. Rarely honored outside enterprise gear.

18.desc: WNM Sleep Mode Request (category 10, action 1). Tells a client to enter a WNM-sleep state. Forged against a client can park it in sleep mode, silently dropping its traffic. Unicast is far more effective than broadcast.

19.desc: WNM Sleep Mode Response (category 10, action 2). Client's reply to a sleep request. Spoofed to the AP to fake sleep-state changes.

20.desc: WNM Timing Measurement Request (category 10, action 16). Used for fine timing measurement (802.11mc ranging). Flooding it wastes client radio cycles.

21.desc: Direct Link Setup Request (category 2, action 0). Predecessor to TDLS. Only meaningful between two STAs on the same BSS; ignored elsewhere.

22.desc: Direct Link Setup Teardown (category 2, action 2). Tear down a DLS link between two STAs. Rare; very few modern devices use DLS.

23.desc: Block Ack Action (category 3, actions 0-3). Setup/teardown of block-ack sessions. Forged ones can disrupt QoS stream aggregation on the target.

24.desc: HT Action (category 7, action 0) — Notify Channel Width. Tells the peer to change HT channel width. Forged frames can force a client into a narrower channel.

25.desc: HT Action (category 7, action 1) — SM Power Save. Puts the peer into spatial-multiplexing power save. Forged against a client reduces its MIMO capability.

26.desc: Mesh Action (category 12, action 0) — HWMP Path Request. Only meaningful on 802.11s mesh. Rare in consumer deployments.

27.desc: Mesh Action (category 12, action 1) — Mesh Peering Open. Mesh-only; can desynchronize peering state on mesh nodes.

28.desc: Mesh Action (category 12, action 2) — Mesh Peering Confirm. Mesh-only.

29.desc: Mesh Action (category 12, action 3) — Mesh Peering Close. Mesh-only; can tear down established mesh links.

30.desc: Self-Protected Action (category 14, action 0). Protected action frames used in mesh/PMF contexts. Rarely seen outside specific mesh setups.

31.desc: DMG Action (category 15). Directional multi-gigabit (60 GHz / 802.11ad) beacon actions. Only relevant to wigig devices.

32.desc: Vendor-Specific Action (category 127). Payload interpretation depends on the OUI. Pick a vendor below.

generic.desc: Rotates OUIs across Cisco/Aruba/Ubiquiti/generic on every frame. Widest coverage against unknown APs.

cisco.desc: Fixed Cisco OUI (00:00:0c). Reaches proprietary Cisco handlers if the target is Cisco.

aruba.desc: Fixed Aruba OUI (00:1a:1e). Reaches Aruba/HP enterprise handlers.

ubiquiti.desc: Fixed Ubiquiti OUI (00:0f:e8). Reaches UniFi handlers.
